summary: Intermittent high RTT and WireGuard tunnel drops correlated with Meraki AP channel-width shifts in SF office
description: Multiple SF office users report sudden increases in WireGuard RTTs (200-800ms) followed by tunnel flaps when connected to the corporate SSID. Issue appears after short periods of normal connectivity and correlates with Meraki AP radio events where channel width is reduced from 40MHz to 20MHz. Impact: developer laptops lose connectivity to internal services; CI jobs fail; remote access sessions time out.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a workstation (Linux, macOS, Windows) to Redwood-corp SSID at SF office AP group A.
2) Establish a WireGuard tunnel to prod gateway and run continuous ping (1s) to 10.12.0.1.
3) From Meraki dashboard, trigger radio reconfiguration: change channel width preference from 40MHz to auto or simulate DFS event on affected channels.
4) Observe RTTs and packet loss on the workstation; check wireguard handshake timestamps and kernel networking counters.
Expected: steady RTT ~15-40ms and stable tunnel. Observed: RTT spikes to 200-800ms, increased retransmits, then handshake timeouts and tunnel re-establishment.
Notes: Reproducible in SF office on APs running Meraki MR44/MR46 firmware v26.7 and v27.x in the same AP group. Not observed when client is wired.
logs: Mar 12 09:14:02 host kernel: wlan0: TX failed, retry limit reached (rc=-110)
Mar 12 09:14:03 wireguard[2342]: handshake with 35.192.10.22:51820 failed: timeout
Meraki event: Radio profile changed: channel width 40->20 on AP MR44 serial ABC123 (event id 75831)
syslog snippets and tcpdump show repeated 802.11 retransmits and 802.11 ack timeouts during the window
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: DFS or auto-channel-selection triggered channel width reduction leading to higher airtime and retransmits under existing client density.
Checked Meraki dashboard: AP group has 'Auto RF' enabled with channel width set to '20/40MHz'. Several APs reported recent DFS events in logs within the same minute as reported client drops.
Captured clients with tcpdump showing elevated 802.11 retransmit rates and aggregated airtime increased from ~15% to ~75% for the radio during the incident window.

WireGuard keepalive period (persistent-keepalive 25s) causes handshakes to overlap retransmit windows and triggers endpoint health checks in the gateway, resulting in temporary routing failover for some services.
Reproduced by forcing radio profile change from dashboard: immediately saw RTT spike and transient packet loss; wired clients unaffected.
Meraki support case opened: SR# 394021 - they confirm firmware in this range changes channel-width behavior more aggressively when Auto RF is enabled and client density increases.
Related internal ticket: INT-9342 has roaming/DHCP drops but different root cause; linked for visibility to wireless team.
Short-term mitigation tested: changing radio profile to force 40MHz where available reduced occurrences in test APs; disabling 802.11r did not change outcome.

Long-term: need coordinated change in Auto RF policy and review of WireGuard keepalive/healthcheck sensitivity; consider gateway tolerance tuning or pinning channel width in high-density office AP groups.
comments: Maya Thompson (reporter) - 2026-03-12: Noticed multiple devs in SF Slack reporting 'internet slow -> internal services unreachable' around 09:13am. Collected packet captures from two affected laptops and uploaded to shared drive (link below).
Liam Chen (assignee) - 2026-03-12: Starting triage. Initial look points to wireless retransmits. Engaging network team and Meraki support. Temporarily disabling Auto RF on a single AP to validate.
Priya Nair (Network Team) - 2026-03-12: Confirmed Meraki events matching timestamps. Filing a Meraki SR; recommend disabling '20/40MHz auto' for SF office AP-group until firmware patch available.

SRE (Ethan Morales) - 2026-03-12: Noted gateway health checks mark endpoints degraded when wireguard RTT > 200ms for 30s. We can relax the health-check threshold as a mitigation but prefer root cause fix.
Maya Thompson - 2026-03-13: Applying forced 40MHz to test APs reduced incidents during morning hours. Still monitoring.

Liam Chen - 2026-03-13: Meraki provided confirmation that firmware v27.0 scheduled to address aggressive width downshifts; PR recommended: update radio profile and schedule controlled firmware rollout.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: network team has applied a temporary radio profile change for SF office AP group to prefer 40MHz and disabled aggressive Auto RF channel-width switching. Meraki SR open; scheduled firmware patch evaluation. SRE to evaluate health-check thresholds for WireGuard to reduce failovers. Final resolution pending Meraki firmware and post-rollout validation.
resolution_notes: Temporary: pinned channel width to 40MHz for primary SF AP group (applied 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC). Observed no further widespread flaps in 24h window on pinned APs.
Planned: Controlled firmware rollouts after Meraki supplies patch; coordinate with Facilities for low-traffic maintenance window.
Follow-up: Update WireGuard health-check grace period to 90s in gateway config to tolerate short RF-induced RTT spikes (change request filed: PR #402).
